# Feature: Interaction Recovery Axes — Wave 1

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-031
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained). Design input: [`.spec-lite/interaction_brainstorm.md`](../../interaction_brainstorm.md) Session 4, Wave 1 (P1–P7).

Make `yantra do` finish an ordinary search form **without the agent having to operate the page by hand**, by fixing the one thing [FEAT-030](../FEAT-030-resilient_browser_interaction/spec.md) did not: recovery that only ever varies _how_ it types, never _where_ the keystrokes go or _what_ query the widget will answer.

The motivating evidence is run `20260829T171218Z-do-0ae073f1` (flight search, DFW↔SJC, December 2026). Unlike its predecessor it **completed and published a good brief** — FEAT-030's disclosure contract, attempt ledgers, and evidence-gated navigation all worked. The cost is the problem: **13.2 minutes, 33 turns, and 14 of those turns spent compensating for tool gaps.**

| Seq   | Call                                                                 | Reported                        | What was actually true                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 14    | `fill_form` "Where from?" = `DFW`                                    | `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` (10.9 s) | All four typing rungs ran against the **closed trigger**; the page routes keystrokes to a **different input inside the overlay the trigger opens**. Every rung varied _how_ to type into a node that was never the editee.                                                                                   |
| 18    | `fill_element` "Where to?" = `SJC`                                   | `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` (8.7 s)  | Same cause. `field stayed empty` three times over.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 22    | `fill_element` `e80` = `San Jose`                                    | `WIDGET_AMBIGUOUS_CHOICE`       | Correct, and correctly reported three offered labels — **this part worked.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 24    | `fill_element` `e80` = `San Jose Mineta International Airport (SJC)` | `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` (13.9 s) | **The retype trap.** The agent obeyed the hint — _"re-issue this call with one of those strings exactly as written"_ — and the full label matched nothing in a prefix-matching autocomplete. The hint named a move the engine has no path for.                                                               |
| 30    | `fill_form` "Departure"                                              | `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE`     | _"No date widget driver recognized 'Departure' with sufficient confidence."_ A bare textbox that reveals its calendar only on click is invisible to closed-state detection. The attached hint told the agent to _"check details.displayedMonths or details.offered"_ — **neither field was in the payload.** |
| 32–52 | 11 × `browser_click`                                                 | all `ok`                        | The agent gave up on the tool and drove the calendar by hand: ~35 s of wall time plus eleven LLM round-trips, doing what `calendarDriver` exists to do in one call.                                                                                                                                          |
| 58    | `fill_element` "Departure"                                           | `WIDGET_DID_NOT_OPEN`           | Same class, opposite symptom.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 62    | `fill_element` "Return"                                              | `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`              | Soft wall-clock, spent almost entirely on the above.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

Also note seq 14: the batch was asked for four fields, failed on the first, and returned `applied: []` — the three remaining fields were never attempted, so a call that existed to make four fields' worth of progress made none.

After this feature: a fill finds the control the page actually edits before deciding it cannot type; a widget that answers prefixes gets a prefix; a hint can only name a move the engine has an engineered path for; a picker that opens on click is driven rather than hand-cranked; and a batch that fails one field still fills the others.

**Non-goal, and the hard constraint on every line of this work:** no website-specific logic (memory → General). Every signal here is structural: observed focus, value flow, ARIA relationships, and what the widget itself offered.

**Explicitly out of scope** (Wave 2, per the brainstorm): declarative escalation plans as a general refactor (P8), the obstruction protocol (P9), page-delta observations (P10), the general copy-hygiene harness (P11), the full Widget Gauntlet (P12), and the opt-in screenshot/vision assist. Wave 1 adds fixtures to the harness FEAT-030 already built rather than starting a new one.

## 2. Technical Context

> Standing rules (TypeScript strictness, ESM, DI, testing, logging, security) are in `.spec-lite/memory.md`. Only additions and overrides appear here.

### Approach

**The organizing idea: recovery varies the question, not just the attempt.** Every rung is typed by axis, and evidence from one axis diverts to another instead of funding more of the same:

- **WHERE** — is this live node the one the page actually edits? (new; TASK-001)
- **WHAT** — what query shape will this widget answer? (new; TASK-002)
- **HOW** — typing mechanics, pacing, native setters. (exists: `interaction/typing.ts`)

Today's ladder is HOW-only, which is why three of the run's failures burned 8–14 s each producing `field stayed empty` three times. The fix is not more rungs; it is **evidence-gated exit from the wrong axis**.

**A. Editee resolution — the WHERE rung** (`interaction/editee.ts`). Before concluding that a control will not take text, ask the page where the text went.

**There is no probe keystroke.** Rung 1 (`port.fill`, `typing.ts:188-190`) has already sent the **whole value**, so by the time this question is worth asking the text is already wherever it was going — and the requested value is itself the needle, far more distinctive than a single character would be. Sending one more character at that point would be a redundant mutation that appends to, and corrupts, a value that already arrived. The work is a **comparison, not an action**: observe, let rung 1 act, observe again, and find the interactable whose value now holds the text.

**It runs in ref-space, not raw DOM.** Refs are minted only by `observe()` (`agent-controller.ts:388-414`), and every consumer — `port.fill`, `port.type`, `readRawValue`, the driver's re-target — addresses elements by ref, so an element discovered through `evaluateOn` has no ref and could not be driven even once found. `AgentInteractable` already carries `value`, and `browser-common.ts:103-111` already converts one into a `WidgetTarget`; diffing `interactables[].value` by ref therefore yields a re-targetable editee **by construction**. `<input>` is in `INTERACTABLE_SELECTOR`, so an overlay's own input is observed as soon as it is on the page.

If the editee is a different live node, the drive re-targets to it and the result reports the substitution the way `tieBreak` already reports a narrowed resolution. Entirely structural — value flow and observed focus, never site shape.

**B. Query shaping — the WHAT rung** (`interaction/query-plan.ts`). One ordered plan per fill: **as-given** → **code token** (an uppercase short token, unifying the behavior the `code-to-label-typeahead` fixture already covers) → **prefix retreat** (when a value yields no suggestions, retreat to a shortened distinguishing prefix). The critical rule: **ranking is always against the full requested value regardless of what was typed.** Typing `"San Jose Mine"` and ranking against `"San Jose Mineta International Airport (SJC)"` is what makes the offered-label hint honest.

**C. The combobox family** (`widgets/combobox/combobox-driver.ts`), per the confirmed decision. `WidgetFamily` gains `'combobox'` and the driver registers in `createDefaultWidgetRegistry()`, so comboboxes get the same `detect()` confidence ordering and fallback chain date and option already have. The driver owns the whole choreography — engage → editee (A) → query plan (B) → settle → rank → select → verify against the chosen option → release. `fill/react.ts`'s `watchAndSelect` becomes the driver's selection stage rather than a parallel implementation, so exactly one typeahead path exists. The engine's plain-text path survives for controls where no combobox is detected and nothing is offered.

**The intent reaching the driver is an option intent, and the engine keeps the free-text decision.** `WidgetIntent` has no `text` member (`widgets/types.ts:74-77`) and gains none here; the engine reuses the existing `asOptionIntent` (`engine.ts:631-635`), which already maps `text` → `{ kind: 'option', value }`. That mapping is lossy — the driver can no longer tell "free text is acceptable if it stands" from "a choice must be made" — so the driver never decides it. On no match the driver reports what was offered and whether the typed text survived release, and the **engine** resolves that into `typed_literal` or a failure, preserving today's `standingText` behavior (`react.ts:186-201`) rather than reimplementing it one layer down.

**D. Failures keyed by (code, cause)** (`fill/types.ts`), internal per the confirmed decision. `FillErrorCode` stays exactly as it is — it is the programmatic contract and the model already reads it. A new internal `FillCause` discriminator selects **message, hint, and required details together**, replacing today's arrangement where `hintFor` infers a hint from which detail fields happen to be present and otherwise falls back to a per-code sentence. That fallback is what produced _"check details.displayedMonths"_ on a failure carrying no months. `cause` never crosses the tool seam; the model continues to see `error_code`, a cause-specific `message`, and `details`.

**Causes are scoped per code, not crossed with every code.** A flat map over `${FillErrorCode}/${FillCause}` would demand all 81 combinations, most of them nonsense (`FILL_VALUE_INVALID/picker-did-not-open`), and forcing prose for 81 entries guarantees the near-duplicates the invariant test exists to forbid. The table nests — each code declares only the causes it can actually produce — and exhaustiveness is checked _within_ each code.

**`reason` is a reserved detail key.** `classifyFailure` overrides the code table on `details.reason === 'budget' | 'disabled'` (`attempt.ts:78-79`), deliberately: `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` is in `TRANSIENT_CODES`, so a budget-exhausted one is terminal _only_ by that key. Every template preserves `reason` verbatim; dropping or renaming it would make budget failures retryable and loop them to the attempt bound — exactly what `withAttempts` exists to prevent.

**E. The actionable-hint invariant** (P4), the reason D is worth doing. Each entry in the new hint table declares two things beside its text: `requiredDetails` (the detail keys its wording references) and `capability` (the exported engine function that makes the advice work). A test enumerates the table and asserts every hint's `requiredDetails` are populated wherever that pair is constructed, and every `capability` resolves to a real export. _"Re-issue with one of those strings"_ is only legal because the combobox driver ships `selectByOfferedLabel`. **A hint with no capability is a failing test, not a code review note.**

Because that test asserts every named capability resolves to a real export, **the table lands after the capabilities it names.** The open-probe is TASK-004 and the template table is TASK-005, not the other way round — a table naming `probeOpen` before `probeOpen` exists would fail its own verification, and the tempting workarounds (a stub, or downgrading the assertion to a warning) would gut the invariant on its first day.

**F. The open-probe stage** (`widgets/open-probe.ts`). The rule "detection never clicks" stays — it is what makes `detect()` safe to run across every registered driver. The probe is a **separate engine-owned stage** that runs only when detection returned nothing above threshold _and_ the intent plus field semantics agree (intent is a date, the control is a textbox with a date-shaped name/placeholder/value). It clicks the trigger once, re-runs detection against the open state, and either drives or dismisses and fails with what it actually saw. One probe per fill, recorded in the ledger.

**G. Batch partial progress** (`browser-fill-form.ts`), per the confirmed decision. A failed field no longer ends the batch. Every remaining field is attempted **except** those belonging to the same widget group as the failed one — a shared range picker or one overlay, where a second attempt would fail for a reason the agent cannot distinguish from a real problem. Dependence is read from observed page structure, never from field ordering.

**Dependence is compared on the observation's `group`, not on a live container.** `applyBrowserFill` calls `bestEffortDismiss` on failure (`browser-fill-element.ts:184-186`), which closes the widget — so `resolveContainer` on the failed field afterwards commonly returns `null`, and a rule written against it would quietly never fire while still passing a unit test that kept the container alive. `AgentInteractable.group` is captured at observation time and survives the dismissal, so that is what the skip rule compares.

**A partial batch stays visible in the audit trail.** The middleware records `status: 'ok'` for any successful `DomainResult` (`middleware.ts:367`), and `report.md` renders one line per call from that projection — the very format this spec's evidence table is built from. A batch returning `ok: true` with two failed fields would otherwise appear as a flat `browser_fill_form - ok`, hiding exactly the kind of defect this feature exists to surface. So the result carries `partial`, `applied_count`, `failed_count`, and `skipped_count` in `details`, and the report writer renders a partial line distinctly.

**H. One real copy bug.** `budget.ts:196` already carries the publish remedy for the soft wall-clock limit, and `middleware.ts:253-255` appends a second, near-identical one for every non-terminal tool — so the agent read the same instruction twice. The remedy belongs to the budget decision that knows whether one is already present. _(An earlier draft of the brainstorm also reported a mojibake em-dash here. Verified against the artifact's raw bytes: it is a correct U+2014 and the mojibake was a Windows PowerShell 5.1 ANSI read artifact. **There is no encoding bug and nothing to fix for it.** The brainstorm has been corrected.)_

**Budget and the fast-fail target.** `defaultWidgetBudget` stays at 25 s — it is the ceiling for a fill making _progress_, and lowering it would break the slow-autocomplete handling FEAT-030 deliberately bought. The ≤4 s target is met by **exiting the wrong axis early**, not by a smaller ceiling: when the editee probe reports keystrokes landing elsewhere, the HOW ladder stops at rung 1 instead of running rungs 2 and 3 into the same wall.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

No overrides to memory's standing rules. Three internal pre-release API changes, which memory permits breaking cleanly:

- **`WidgetFamily` gains `'combobox'`.** A closed union in `widgets/types.ts`; every `switch` over it is updated in the same task.
- **`fillFailure()` gains a required `cause` argument.** Every call site in `packages/core/src/fill/` and `widgets/` is updated in TASK-005. The emitted `FillFailure` shape is unchanged, so the tool seam and `tool-calls.jsonl` projection are untouched.
- **`AttemptRecord` gains `axis: 'where' | 'what' | 'how'`.** Additive and non-breaking. The three axes are the organizing idea of this feature and currently exist only as prose; naming the axis on the record makes "which axis did this run waste time on" answerable straight from `tool-calls.jsonl`, and makes Wave 2's declarative escalation plans (P8) a **re-grouping of data that already exists** rather than a redesign.

**`WidgetIntent` is deliberately _not_ widened.** The combobox driver receives an option intent via the existing `asOptionIntent`; see §2C for why the free-text decision stays in the engine.

`PROMPT_VERSION` stays `agent-v8` and `AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT` stays byte-identical — tool descriptions and the `do` addendum change, `tool_catalog_hash` moves, and the manifest already records it. Same discipline as FEAT-030.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

N/A — no relational data model, no persisted entities, no schema migration. `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist and is not needed.

The durable shapes are **tool-result contracts**, recorded per call in `tool-calls.jsonl`. Wave 1 changes three and adds one internal type:

**`FillCause`** (`fill/types.ts`, **internal — never serialized to the model**) — the discriminator that, **scoped per error code** (§2D), selects message, hint, and required details:

- `keystrokes-landed-elsewhere` — the editee probe found a different live editee
- `value-rejected-on-release` — the control cleared the typed text when the widget closed
- `no-suggestion-matched` — the widget offered a list, none matched, text did not stand
- `typing-exhausted` — every HOW rung ran against the confirmed editee
- `driver-not-recognized` — no driver above threshold, and the open-probe did not change that
- `value-not-offered` — a driver ran and the value is not among what the widget offers
- `picker-did-not-open` — a trigger exposed no container within the wait
- `element-replaced` — the page re-mounted the control faster than re-acquisition
- `budget` — a bound was reached before the work completed

**`AppliedBrowserFill`** (`browser-fill-element.ts`) gains `editee?: { ref, name, role }` — present only when the drive re-targeted, so a caller can see which control was actually edited.

**`browser_fill_form` result** replaces `applied[]`-only with three sets:

- `applied[]` — as today, each with `requested` / `committed` / `resolution`
- `failed[]` — `{ field, error_code, message, observed?, offered?, attempted? }`
- `skipped[]` — `{ field, reason: 'same-widget-group-as-failed', blocked_by: <field> }`

plus, in `details` (so the audit projection can see it): `partial` (true when `applied` and `failed` are both non-empty), `applied_count`, `failed_count`, `skipped_count`.

**`AttemptRecord`** gains `axis: 'where' | 'what' | 'how'` alongside `strategy`, which gains the Wave 1 rung names:

| `strategy`                                                                              | `axis`  |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `locate-editee`, `retarget-editee`                                                      | `where` |
| `query:as-given`, `query:code-token`, `query:prefix-retreat`, `select-by-offered-label` | `what`  |
| `overtype`, `clear-then-type`, `native-setter` (existing)                               | `how`   |
| `open-probe`, `driver:combobox`, `driver:*` (existing)                                  | `how`   |

## 6. Implementation Tasks

### TASK-001: Editee resolution — find the control the page actually edits

- [x] **Implementation**: Add `axis: 'where' | 'what' | 'how'` to `AttemptRecord` (`interaction/types.ts`) and set it on every existing rung per the §3 table — `overtype` / `clear-then-type` / `native-setter` are `how`.
      Create `packages/core/src/interaction/editee.ts` exporting `locateEditee(before, after, target, requested): EditeeResolution` where `EditeeResolution` is `{ kind: 'same' } | { kind: 'delegated', target: WidgetTarget, evidence: EditeeEvidence } | { kind: 'inert', evidence: EditeeEvidence }`.
      **It takes two observations and performs no action.** `before` and `after` are `AgentBrowserObservation`s; the function diffs `interactables[].value` **by ref** and finds which interactable now holds `requested`. This keeps the whole thing in ref-space: refs are minted only by `observe()` (`agent-controller.ts:388-414`), so an element found via `evaluateOn` would have no ref and could not be driven. Build the delegated `WidgetTarget` from the matching `AgentInteractable` exactly as `browser-common.ts:103-111` already does. Being a pure function of two observations, it is also directly unit-testable with no port at all.
      Classify: the target's own value now holds the text → `same`; exactly one _other_ interactable's value changed to hold it → `delegated`; nothing changed anywhere → `inert`; **more than one** other interactable changed → `inert`, never a guess. `evidence` records which signal fired (`value-appeared-elsewhere`, `focus-moved`, `none`), and is recorded in the ledger on **success as well as failure**, so the classifier can be tuned later from run artifacts at no extra cost — it is a fixed enum carrying no page text.
      In `interaction/typing.ts`, `commitText` gains an optional editee hook: when rung 1's readback is empty, take a fresh observation, call `locateEditee`, and on `delegated` return a typed failure carrying the delegated target **without running rungs 2 and 3**; `inert` continues the ladder as today. **The ladder's `classify` must become cause-aware** — it is currently `classify: () => 'transient'` (`typing.ts:166`), which would retry the delegated exit straight into rung 2 and silently negate the fast-fail. Delegated is terminal; every other rung failure stays transient by construction.
      The caller (`fill/engine.ts`) re-targets to the delegated editee and drives it. Nothing here reads a hostname, brand, or selector table.
- [x] **Unit Tests**: `packages/core/tests/interaction/editee.spec.ts` — pure-function tests over observation pairs, no port needed. Cover: the target stays empty while one overlay interactable's value becomes the requested text → `delegated` naming that ref, `evidence: 'value-appeared-elsewhere'` (**the run's seq-14/18/24 shape**); the target itself holds the text → `same`; nothing changed anywhere → `inert`; **two** other interactables changed → `inert`, not a guess; an interactable present in `after` but absent from `before` (the overlay's input, newly observed) is still eligible as the delegated editee.
      Extend `tests/interaction/typing.spec.ts` against a **call-counting port**: an empty rung-1 readback plus a `delegated` editee invokes `applyStrategy` **exactly once** — asserted by call count, not merely by ledger length, since a ledger with one record would also result from a retry that failed to record; the ledger entry carries `axis: 'where'`; an `inert` editee still escalates through all three rungs exactly as today; a delegated exit is classified terminal by the ladder's `classify`.

- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- interaction/editee interaction/typing` passes; `pnpm --filter @yantra/core typecheck` clean; the existing typing-ladder assertions from FEAT-030 pass unmodified; `locateEditee` imports nothing from `widgets/` beyond types.

### TASK-002: Query shaping and the select-by-offered-label fast path

- [x] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/interaction/query-plan.ts` — **pure string and ranking logic, no widget-layer imports**, so it needs no port to test.
      `shapeQuery(requested: string): readonly QueryForm[]` returns the ordered plan, each form `{ kind: 'as-given' | 'code-token' | 'prefix-retreat', text: string }`. `code-token` is emitted when the request contains a short all-caps token (the shape the existing `code-to-label-typeahead` fixture covers) — that token alone. `prefix-retreat` is the longest leading run of word characters that stays under a length bound.
      **`shapeQuery` generates; the driver consumes lazily.** All applicable forms are returned up front — a pure function of a string cannot know what a page offered — and the driver walks them in order, stopping at the first that yields candidates. "Only used when earlier forms found nothing" is a consumption rule, not an emission rule.
      `rankAgainstRequested(candidates, requested)` is the invariant that matters: **ranking always compares against the full requested value**, never against the shortened text that was typed. It is the single ranking entry point the combobox driver uses, so the two cannot drift.
      `selectByOfferedLabel` is specified here but **implemented alongside the combobox driver in TASK-003** — it needs `collectCandidates`/`clickCandidate` and would drag the widget layer into this module. Its contract: derive a distinguishing prefix of `label`, type that, settle, and click the candidate whose name matches `label` — **never retype the full label into a prefix matcher.** This is the capability that makes the offered-label hint honest.
- [x] **Unit Tests**: `packages/core/tests/interaction/query-plan.spec.ts` — pure-function tests only; the fixture-driven end-to-end case lives in TASK-003 where a port exists. Cover: `"San Jose Mineta International Airport (SJC)"` → a `prefix-retreat` form whose text is a genuine prefix, short enough to match a prefix matcher; `"SJC"` → `code-token` emitted before `prefix-retreat`; a plain short value → only `as-given`, no wasted forms; `rankAgainstRequested` selects the full-label candidate when the _typed_ text was only a prefix (**the ranking half of the run's seq-24 retype trap**); ranking is stable and returns `ambiguous` on a genuine tie.
- [x] **Documentation Update**: None — behavior is visible through TASK-003.
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- interaction/query-plan` passes; `query-plan.ts` imports nothing from `widgets/` (asserted in the existing boundary suite); ranking has exactly one implementation.

### TASK-003: The combobox driver family

- [x] **Implementation**: Add `'combobox'` to `WidgetFamily` (`widgets/types.ts`) and update every exhaustive switch.

Export `scoreComboboxShape(element)` as a **named function separate from `detect()`**, so the gauntlet can test detection independently of driving — detection errors and driving errors have entirely different fixes and are today distinguishable only by reading a ledger. ### TASK-005: Failures keyed by (code, cause), with the hint-capability invariant

- [x] **Implementation**: In `fill/types.ts` add the internal `FillCause` discriminator (§3) and replace `FILL_FAILURE_HINTS` + `hintFor` with a **table nested by code**, not a flat cross-product:

```ts
const FAILURE_TEMPLATES = {
  WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED: {
    'keystrokes-landed-elsewhere': { … },
    'typing-exhausted': { … },
    'value-rejected-on-release': { … },
  },
  WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE: { 'driver-not-recognized': { … }, 'value-not-offered': { … }, … },
  // … only the causes each code can actually produce
} as const satisfies FailureTemplateTable;
```

      A flat `Record<`${FillErrorCode}/${FillCause}`, …>` would demand all 81 combinations, most of them nonsense (`FILL_VALUE_INVALID/picker-did-not-open`), and writing 81 templates guarantees the near-duplicates assertion (c) exists to forbid. Exhaustiveness is checked **within** each code.
      `FailureTemplate = { message(details), hint, requiredDetails: readonly string[], capability: string | null }`. `capability` names the exported engine function that makes the advice work (`'selectByOfferedLabel'`, `'probeOpen'`, `'locateEditee'`, …) and is `null` only for hints that advise *observation* rather than a retry. Every capability named here already exists: TASK-003 and TASK-004 ship them.
      Change `fillFailure(errorCode, cause, message, details, retryable)` and update every call site in `fill/` and `widgets/`, including the open-probe failures from TASK-004. **`cause` selects the template and is then dropped** — it must not appear in the emitted `FillFailure`, so the tool seam and `tool-calls.jsonl` projection stay byte-compatible.
      **`reason` is a reserved detail key preserved verbatim by every template** (§2D): `classifyFailure` overrides the code table on `details.reason === 'budget' | 'disabled'` (`attempt.ts:78-79`), and since `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED` is in `TRANSIENT_CODES`, dropping it would make a budget-exhausted failure retryable and loop it to the attempt bound.
      Delete the per-code fallback sentence entirely: a `(code, cause)` pair with no template is a compile error, not a generic string. This is what removes *"check details.displayedMonths"* from a failure that has no months.
      Separately, fix the duplicated budget remedy: move the publish sentence out of `middleware.ts:253-255` and append it only when the budget decision's own message does not already carry one (`budget.ts:196`, `wall-clock-soft`, does). *(No encoding fix — verified there is no mojibake; see §2H.)*

Plus: for every template whose cause is `budget`, `classifyFailure(code, details)` returns `'terminal'` — the regression guard for the reserved key; `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE/driver-not-recognized` and `.../value-not-offered` read differently (**the run's seq-30 wrong-hint bug**); `WIDGET_NOT_COMMITTED/keystrokes-landed-elsewhere` and `.../typing-exhausted` read differently; the emitted `FillFailure` contains **no** `cause` key. Extend `packages/agent/tests/runtime/middleware.spec.ts` + `budget.spec.ts`: a soft wall-clock refusal contains the publish instruction exactly once; a per-tool budget refusal still carries it once.

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth / secrets**: Unchanged and explicitly protected. `fillSecretField` keeps `allowEscalation: false`, and **editee resolution is not available to secrets** — locating the editee means searching observations for the value that was sent, which for a credential is a readback of secret-derived state and would place it in a comparison against every observed interactable. `locateEditee` is therefore reachable only from the non-secret path, asserted by a test that a secret fill performs no second observation and no readback. Host binding, `withSecret` disposal, and the no-suggestion-discovery rule are untouched.
- **Error Handling**: No new error codes. `FillErrorCode` is unchanged; `FillCause` is internal and never serialized. `classifyFailure` stays total over the code union so a new pair cannot be silently treated as transient and loop, and `details.reason` is preserved verbatim by every template so its budget/disabled override keeps working (§2D). The typing ladder's `classify` becomes cause-aware rather than unconditionally transient, so the delegated-editee exit is terminal and is not retried into the rung it exists to skip. Nothing is swallowed — the open-probe always dismisses what it opened before failing, and `withAttempts` still returns the last failure with the full ledger.
- **Logging**: New `AttemptRecord.strategy` values ride the existing sanitized `tool-calls.jsonl` projection — no new sink, no new artifact. `EditeeEvidence` is a fixed enum of structural signal names, never page text, so it carries nothing to redact. The delegated editee's `name`/`role` are page-derived and pass the same sanitizer as every other observation field.
- **Security / Privacy**: No new network egress, no new host, no change to URL provenance, the ethics gate, consent, or budgets. `offered[]` stays capped at 10. The open-probe issues one click on a control the caller already addressed — no navigation, no form submission — and dismisses whatever it opened.
- **Determinism / replay**: Saved-workflow replay stays LLM-free. Replayed `fill_element` steps route through the same engine and inherit editee resolution, query shaping, the combobox driver, and the open-probe, which makes replay more robust **without letting a model steer it** — the trace records the semantic fill, never a driver choice, an editee, or a query form, so nothing model-derived enters the plan. Scheduled and nested `workflow_run` runs remain hard zero-LLM.
- **Performance**: Editee resolution costs one extra `observe()` (bounded by the existing `FILL_RESOLUTION_CAP`) and no page actions at all, spent only on the rung-1-empty path where it replaces two typing rungs costing 1–5 s — so it **reduces** wall time on exactly the path that was slowest. The open-probe costs one click plus the existing `OPEN_WAIT_MS` bound, spent only where the alternative today is an outright failure. If observation cost later shows up in run timings, a value-only re-projection is the escape hatch (tracked in `TODO.md`); measure before optimizing.
